title: SCE authoring profile (wire schema v1)
description: What a specification owner configures about how documents are authored for them: a file beside the specification, read by `sce-codegen check --profile`, `generate --profile` and `orchestrate --profile` and by the authoring MCP, and pinned by an acceptance record as part of what a design was authored from. It is data, never code, and names no subject matter. Every setting belongs to ONE class, fixed by this schema and not by the file: enforced (a draft that breaks it is refused), reported (a departure is listed and the owner decides), or guidance (handed to the author, checked by nothing). A build that meets a setting it does not know refuses the whole profile, so a profile written for a newer tool is never half applied; a setting is added without a version bump. A setting applies to statecharts, and `evidence` and `names` reach the forge documents they name; a forge document that no setting reaches is not judged. Authoritative reader is sce-build/src/authoring_profile.rs. The stability status of this surface lives in this header alone — see SCE_WIRE_CONTRACTS.md.

style.description: A spelling convention for one token of a name, ASCII only: `snake` (door_open), `upper_snake` (DOOR_OPEN), `camel` (doorOpen), `pascal` (DoorOpen), `kebab` (door-open) or `lower` (dooropen). A capital letter in `camel` and `pascal` starts a word and is followed by a lower-case letter or a digit, so an acronym is spelled as a word (`doorHttp`, not `doorHTTP`).

word.description: One word: letters and digits, compared without regard to case against the words a name is made of (`doorOpen`, `door_open` and `DOOR-OPEN` are made of `door` and `open`).

nameRule.description: What a name of one class must satisfy. Every entry is optional and a rule states at least one.

max_length.description: The longest a whole name may be, in characters.

forbidden_words.description: Words no name of this class is made of.

required_prefix.description: What every name of this class begins with, exactly as spelled.

eventRule.description: A `nameRule` for event names, whose `style` applies to each dot-separated token, with the structure of an event name.

tokens.description: How many dot-separated tokens an event name has, at both ends inclusive; one end may be left out.

first_tokens.description: The tokens an event name may begin with, such as the subject of a `subject.verb` structure.

prefix_free.description: `true`: no event name of the document is a token prefix of another. W3C SCXML 3.12.1 matches a descriptor by token prefix, so a transition on `door` also takes `door.open`; this keeps a name from taking what was meant for another.

record.description: Names the kind of file, so a JSON document of another kind is refused before its settings are read.

v.description: Schema version. Bumped only on a breaking shape change; a setting is added without a bump.

name.description: A label a report may print. Not a setting: it configures nothing, and it is part of the file's bytes like every other character, so renaming a profile is a new profile to an acceptance record.

interface.description: ENFORCED. `closed`: every statechart declares `sce:interface="closed"`, so it takes and sends only the events its imported event-schemas declare (docs/SCE_ACCEPTED_SUBSET.md §2.16) and the boundary the owner accepted is the one it is held to. A statechart that does not is refused as `profile/interface-not-closed`. Absent: the interface is not constrained, and a statechart that leaves it open is the owner's choice.

names.description: ENFORCED. How the names a document DEFINES are spelled, by class: `document` (the `name` of the `<scxml>` root), `state` (the id of a state, parallel, final or history), `event` (an event the document raises, sends or takes by a literal name) and `data` (a `<data>` id). An event-schema document is judged too: the event it declares (`sce:event-name`) is class `event`, and the ids of its fields are class `data`, since that is where a boundary event is spelled once. A statechart is not judged for a name it takes from an imported event-schema, nor for the platform's own `error.*` and `done.*`, since those are not its author's choice; a name that starts with an underscore belongs to the platform. A draft that breaks a rule is refused as `profile/name-style`, `profile/name-limit`, `profile/event-structure` or `profile/event-prefix-of-another`, each naming the rule.

evidence.description: ENFORCED. `anchored`: every `<sce:evidence>` of a document's `<sce:kind-basis>`, in a statechart or in a forge document of any kind, names where the specification states what it cites, in the `sce:provenance` form. An unanchored one is refused as `profile/evidence-unanchored`. Absent: an evidence may stand without an anchor.

house_rules.description: REPORTED. The owner's standing answers to gaps that recur across specifications — what a draft does where the specification is silent, decided once: `an event a state does not mention is ignored`, `the initial state is the first condition the specification lists`. A draft that applies one does not ask, and cites it by its id: `sce:assumed="<id>"` on the element it applies to. Every citation is listed in the run's `open` (a `house-rule` entry) and marked `house_rule` in the `unresolved` records, so a rule is never applied silently, and it is not counted among the values chosen without an answer. The authoring core's `decisions` check licenses the citation the way it licenses a decision's. What nothing here can see is a rule applied WITHOUT its citation: a rule is prose, and no check reads a document's behaviour against prose. An id names one rule.

id.description: What a draft writes in `sce:assumed` to cite the rule: one token, since a marker id holds no space.

rule.description: The rule, in the owner's words.

guidance.description: GUIDANCE. Standing instructions to whoever writes the document — how to ask, what language the comments are in, what to do where the specification is silent. Handed over as written and checked by NOTHING: the product cannot see the conversation, and a run under a profile that has guidance says how many entries it handed over and that none was checked.
